headline: Egypt demands probe into referee's controversial decisions in Argentina match
summary: Controversy erupts as Egypt's second goal is overturned by VAR, while Argentina's third goal stands despite a penalty claim by Mohamed Salah.
details: Argentina has secured a place in the quarter-finals of the FIFA World Cup, but the match against Egypt has been overshadowed by allegations of refereeing bias.

The controversy centers on two key moments: Egypt's second goal was disallowed after VAR reviewed a slight touch on Lisandro Martinez, while Argentina's third goal was allowed despite Mohamed Salah being fouled in the box during the build-up.
Egyptian players have accused the referee of favoritism, questioning why VAR was not used to check Salah's penalty claim before Argentina's counter-attack led to a goal.

According to FIFA rules, a foul is called if a player steps on an opponent's foot based on intensity and intent; the referee deemed the touch on Martinez as a careless foul, leading to the the goal's cancellation.

In the case of Salah's penalty claim, rules state that if a defender first clearly touches the ball during a tackle, subsequent physical contact is not a foul. However, the core dispute is the inconsistency in VAR usage.
This is not the first time such issues have arisen; a similar foul was ignored by the referee in a match against Austria, which led to a goal by Mac Allister.
The repeated occurrences of these controversial decisions have led to intense scrutiny of both the match officials and FIFA's regulatory body.
caption:
Why was Egypt's goal cancelled while Argentina's stood? Controversy erupts over 'biased' refereeing in the World Cup.

Argentina has secured a place in the quarter-finals of the FIFA World Cup, but the match against Egypt has been overshadowed by allegations of refereeing bias.

The controversy centers on two key moments: Egypt's second goal was disallowed after VAR reviewed a slight touch on Lisandro Martinez, while Argentina's third goal was allowed despite Mohamed Salah being fouled in the box during the build-up.

Egyptian players have accused the referee of favoritism, questioning why VAR was not used to check Salah's penalty claim before Argentina's counter-attack led to a goal.

According to FIFA rules, a foul is called if a player steps on an opponent's foot based on intensity and intent; the referee deemed the touch on Martinez as a careless foul, leading to the the goal's cancellation.

In the case of Salah's penalty claim, rules state that if a defender first clearly touches the ball during a tackle, subsequent physical contact is not a foul. However, the core dispute is the inconsistency in VAR usage.

This is not the first time such issues have arisen; a similar foul was ignored by the referee in a match against Austria, which led to a goal by Mac Allister.

The repeated occurrences of these controversial decisions have led to intense scrutiny of both the match officials and FIFA's regulatory body.

Source: Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo, Somoy News

headline: Chattogram Board postpones HSC and equivalent exams for all districts
summary: The decision affects students across all districts under the Chattogram Education Board's jurisdiction.
details: The Chattogram Education Board has officially postponed the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations scheduled for Wednesday.
The postponement applies to all districts falling under the jurisdiction of the Chattogram Board.
Students and educational institutions have been notified of the change in schedule.
A new date for the postponed examinations will be announced by the board in due course.
caption:
HSC exams postponed in Chattogram! All districts under the board are affected.

The Chattogram Education Board has officially postponed the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations scheduled for Wednesday.

The postponement applies to all districts falling under the jurisdiction of the Chattogram Board.

Students and educational institutions have been notified of the change in schedule.

A new date for the postponed examinations will be announced by the board in due course.
